“When color is more than pigment—it is power.” Chromatic Dragons are iconic, color-coded elemental dragons known throughout the multiverse for their unique energy alignments and devastating breath weapons. Each dragon’s abilities, demeanor, and social ties are shaped by its color, forming a complex web of rivalries and alliances.

•Magic: Banishment spell, exorcism tech, or custom runes can send them away (DC 20+). •Force: If reduced to 0 HP and their form isn't sustained, they vanish unless anchored. •Disruption: Removing their elemental source (water drained, fire doused, earth scattered) often weakens or banishes them.

Elementals can sometimes be reasoned with—especially those born in sentient realities or summoned intentionally. Use the following interaction rules: •Empathy/Persuasion DCs: Start high (DC 25+), reduced if speaking in their tongue or showing reverence to their element. •Trade: Some Elementals may trade resources, knowledge, or assistance for elemental offerings or help restoring their realm. •Taming: Sentient or semi-sentient Elementals may be bound to a pact or contract, functioning similarly to mounts, companions, or war machines. Requires custom XP abilities or gear.

- Lurking Presence: Can manifest unsettling phenomena (like cold spots, whispers, or eerie images) in its vicinity to unnerve others. Creatures within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 12) or gain disadvantage on attacks and Perception checks due to distraction. - Fear Manifestation: Can invoke memories or fears of a creature it haunts, forcing the target to make a Wisdom save (DC 15) or be frightened for 1 minute. - Frightening Visage: Once per day, the haunting spirit can reveal its true form to instill terror, forcing creatures within 10 feet to make a Wisdom save (DC 13) or become paralyzed with fear for 1 minute.
Prefers to wait for the precise moment to strike. Its neurotoxin numbs the mind first, then the body. Sometimes mistaken for large twisted vines.
Initiative Acts on ownerʼs initiative (can take turn before or after) HP 50% of creatureʼs HP if bound/summoned; full if native XP Cost May require 200–600 XP to bind, based on power

records.proposedName: Rules for Using Incorporeals as Allies
records.summary: Incorporeals can be summoned, bound, or allied through rituals, class features, spells, or pacts. When used as companions or familiars: •Control: They may be player-controlled under specific rules (GM discretion) or act as autonomous NPCs with directives. •Manifestation: Most incorporeals require a mana, flux, or psionic upkeep if they are not native to the environment. •Anchoring: Long-term allies must be bound to a focus or anchor item (e.g., a totem, relic, circuit, crystal). •Dismissal: A dismissed or disrupted incorporeal ally returns to its plane or state and must be resummoned.
Upon taking damage, may explode into shards, teleport 30 ft., and reform. The explosion deals 1d6 force damage in a 10 ft. radius (DC 12 Dex save for half). 🌬 Drift Current (Aetherial – CR 2)

•Treat this as a battlefield + environmental boss. The terrain changes should feel alive and oppressive, not just mechanical. •Use narrative pacing between Bloomstep expansions. The players must feel the Bloom growing in power. •Add weakness nodes—ritual circles, leyline caps, or planar anchors that can be used to delay propagation or suppress a zone for a round.

•Godseed Fragment: A minor reality-manipulating artifact, unstable unless attuned. •Spiral Petal: Can be brewed into a potion that gives one use of time stop or minor multiversal drift. •Rewriting Bloom: If harvested, grants permanent access to a single 1st-level spell that can be cast without components 1/day.

The Bloom reshapes the battlefield into a series of 30 ft. wide rings, expanding outward from its center. Each zone applies cumulative and escalating effects. When a new outer zone appears, the inner zones evolve, becoming more hazardous. 🔵 Zone I – Core of Becoming(0–30 ft) •Stage 1: Terrain is Difficult and twisting. Movement costs double. •Stage 2:(When Zone II manifests) Creatures take 1d10 force damage at start of turn if they moved during that turn. •Stage 3+:(Zone III or beyond) Creatures must succeed on a DC 18 Wisdom save at start of turn or act last in initiative that round. 🟣 Zone II – Prism-Veil Bloom(30–60 ft) •Visuals fracture: All ranged attacks have disadvantage. •Spells cast in this area require a DC 16 Arcana check. On failure, the spell fizzles (no slot loss). •Psychic Noise: Any failed saving throw causes the creature to take 1d6 psychic damage. 🔶 Zone III – Temporal Spiral(60–90 ft) •Time distortion causes initiative to reverse at the start of each round (GM reverses all turn order). •All reactions are suppressed. •The Bloomʼs regeneration is doubled while this zone is active. •If a creature casts the same spell twice within 3 rounds, the second casting backfires (save vs. own DC). 🔺 Zone IV – Symmetry Unfolding(90–120 ft) •All creatures spawn Mirror Echoes when taking damage (AC 12, 1 HP clones, mimic one attack). •Reality stutters: movement is random. Each move action requires a d4: ◦ 1–2: Move as intended ◦ 3: Move in a random direction ◦ 4: Teleport to another point within the same zone (GM decides) 🔻 Zone V – Gravity Coil Bloom(120–150 ft) •Gravity collapses. All flying is disabled. •Creatures must succeed on a DC 18 Strength save at the start of their turn or fall Prone. •Jumping and climb speeds halved. Line-of-sight reduced to 30 ft. due to lensing. 🔴 Zone VI – Logic Spiral Collapse(150–180 ft, final)* •Laws of causality dissolve. At the end of each turn, roll a d6:
Guards crypts, watchposts, and sacred lies. Designed to awaken only when deception is nearby.

•Fragmented Identity: The Insfell cannot be affected by Zone of Truth, Detect Thoughts, or similar effects—it has no real thoughts left. •Crisis Echo: When dropped to 0 HP, it stammers out a final scripted message and explodes into distorted sound and glitch-light. All creatures within 10 ft. make a DC 14 INT save or lose 1d4 memory tags (lose proficiencies, names, or spell prep for 1 hour).
•Shed Reflex: If it would take a critical hit, it can shed part of its body to reduce damage by half. This removes 5 ft. of movement until the end of its next turn.

•It refers to itself in the third person. •It asks imaginary "chat" questions during combat: “Wanna see me do it again, chat?” •If anyone interacts, it assumes the person is a fan and tries to "duet" with them… violently.

At the start of combat or when reduced to 0 HP, the Shedborn Horror vomits out a new body. It regains full HP once per day in this way. Each new body is more grotesque; increase its Strength or Dexterity by +1 each time.
Creatures seeing the transformation must make a Sanity Save (DC 15) or lose 1 Sanity and become frightened for 1 round.
A beacon of forest silence, wrapped in drifting fog and starfire glimmers. Starborne Wisps pass unseen, save for glowing motes and whispered winds. Type: Fey (Mistkin)
Once per rest, summon and hurl 3 oversized props at a target. Each deals 1d8 bludgeoning. If the target fails a DC 13 DEX save, theyʼre knocked prone.
1/day: Delay the consequences of a failed save or lethal effect by 1 round, just long enough for the “next episode.”
Once per rest, release a 15 ft emotional wave. Choose: fear (frightened), joy (disadvantage to resist charm), or sorrow (difficult terrain). DC 13 WIS save to resist.
You make squeaky/fart noises while walking. Stealth imposes disadvantage, but may cause enemies to laugh (DC 10). 15 Theme Music Aura Music follows you. Allies within 10 ft gain +1 to initiative.
Self-aware toons who break the meta and interact with the audience or rules.
Once per rest, if three or more allies join your gag, bit, or performance (e.g., singing a chorus, playing along with a sketch), gain 1 inspiration and temporary HP equal to your level.
Once per rest, clear all effects on yourself (positive and negative). Then roll a d4: on a 1, forget the last round entirely—your actions and impact are erased (GM decides results).
Drawn beings that exist between panels and ink lines.

When reduced to 0 HP, a toon does not die normally. Instead, they are: •Erased, popped, splattered, exploded into confetti, or otherwise “taken out of the scene.” •Restored only through toon-logic methods: being redrawn, rebooted, laughed back to life, etc. Some toons leave dramatic exits, others vanish with comedic flair.
Toons trapped in repetition, reruns, or recursive scenes.
Rhythm governs your motion. You attack, move, and act in tempo.
Toons guided and protected by plot structure and destiny.

If disbelief collapse occurs three times in a single session or scene, the toon begins to "fade" (losing color, outline, or control). Only narrative reintegration (a gag that lands, a laugh, audience attention) can reverse the fading.
If your last attack missed, you may repeat it immediately with advantage.
Elastic, indestructible, slapstick-kinetic toons.
Free Action: Teleport 30 ft to any visible or narratively convenient space—even through walls—if itʼs funnier or stranger that way.
